_meta.note: Industry, peers, street, ownership, moat, critiques, gaps and conflicts for Anthem Biosciences. Only material published on or before 30-Sep-2026.

drivers: Innovators outsource more research, development and manufacturing (asset-light models)
Biologics, ADCs, peptides and oligonucleotides need specialised capability
Emerging biotechs (most of the clinical pipeline) own no plants; biotech funding recovered ~50% YoY in Jan-Apr 2026 (Anthem CFO)
China+1 and the US BIOSECURE Act push work to India
GLP-1 peptides (semaglutide's Indian patent expired in Mar-2026) create demand for domestic API
Patent expiries of >USD300 bn of drugs in 2025-30 (biosimilars, generics)

brokers.thesis: Initiation: 'high-growth Indian CRDMO' with the highest EBITDA margin and ROCE among Indian CRDMOs; fermentation-based peptide capability as a moat; revenue/PAT CAGR 18%/20% FY26-29E; 10% premium to the sector's ~60x forward P/E; flags top-two projects >30% of FY26 sales and Davos ~15%
brokers.epsNote: FY27-28E derived from Jefferies' stated EPS growth of 18% and 15% on FY26 EPS of Rs10.4; FY29E Rs17.9 as stated

brokers.thesis: 'Weak Q1; FY27 growth outlook remains unchanged': deferred shipments recovered over Q2-Q4; revenue/EBITDA/PAT CAGR ~21%/22%/19% FY26-28E; semaglutide API on CDSCO approval; estimates unchanged

In-line quarter, gross margin at its highs (CRDMO 68%); FY27 20% sales guidance read as retained; EBITDA margin cut 200-440bp for Unit IV start-up costs; 57x is a little below the 58x one-year-forward mean

moat.evidence: One of few Indian CRDMOs doing chemistry and biology from discovery to commercial supply; 100+ early programmes feed 10 Phase III and 14 commercial molecules; all four FY26 Phase III additions came from its own funnel

Flow chemistry, biocatalysis, biotransformation, fermentation; gross margin 65% in Q1FY27 after backward integration; company EBITDA margin above 40%, the highest among listed Indian CRDMOs (Jefferies)
USFDA, PMDA, TGA, ANVISA approvals; four USFDA approvals at Unit I and two clean audits at Unit II; no warning letter disclosed
A filed supplier is costly to change for the life of a molecule, but big pharma acquirers re-evaluate suppliers and can dual-source; 14 commercial molecules carry 61% of revenue
425 KL of custom synthesis vs several thousand KL at Divi's or Laurus; Unit IV only doubles it by FY28-29; cannot bid for large commercial volumes or big biologics
Top three customers 56.7% of FY26 revenue (61.2% in FY25); top two molecules 36-38% (Nomura); one US BD partner (Davos) brings ~14%

critiques: Bear: three customers are 57% of revenue and two molecules ~37%; a Phase III failure and a product withdrawal cut FY23 revenue 14%, and Q3FY26/Q1FY27 showed how deferrals swing quarters by 15-25%.
Bear: FY26 growth (15%) missed the 20% management first guided, and FY27 started at -23%; management now refuses to give a number.
Bear: at ~82x trailing and ~60x our FY28E EPS the stock prices in years of 20%+ growth; the DCF does not support the price.
Bear: the free float is small (~29%) and the promoter group has been selling (IPO, Jun-2026 block); the 18-month promoter lock-in ends around Jan-2027.
Bear: other income (~15-20% of PBT) rests on NBFC bonds and FX gains; treasury yields are falling.
Bull: margins are the best in Indian CRDMO and rose through a revenue dip (Q1FY27 gross margin 65%, +780bp YoY), so the economics do not depend on volume.
Bull: four molecules went commercial in FY26 (8-9% of revenue already), 10 are in Phase III with ADCs among them, and two big pharmas were added directly in FY26 plus a third in Q1FY27.
Bull: ~Rs1,720 cr of net cash (Jun-2026) funds the Rs1,200 cr Unit IV without debt or dilution; semaglutide API and a US biosimilar are new legs from FY27.
gaps: Names of customers A-C and of the top molecules are not disclosed; JM names AbbVie, Novartis and Pfizer as clients, but we cannot map them to revenue
Molecule-level revenue: only JM's FY25 table (P-1 USD48 mn, P-2 USD35 mn) and Nomura's top-two share (36-38%); we use them as indicative
Phase mix of the 100+ early-stage programmes (Phase I vs II) is not disclosed
Exact fermentation capacity: RHP table 182 KL after Unit III; Q4 call 180 KL; Q1FY27 deck still shows 142 KL (Mar-2025 figure)
FY23 exceptional gain of Rs54 cr (Screener) is not explained in the documents we read

Broker notes we could not read: DRChoksey (Trendlyne PDF returns 403 to automated access), HDFC Securities Jan-2026 CRDMO initiation (static.hdfcsec.com returns 403), Citi, Kotak, Motilal Oswal, Elara, Nuvama; any JPMorgan or Nomura update after Q4FY26 is unverified

R&D (discovery) and development revenue split for FY26 is only given as ~8-9% and ~15% (CFO); we take R&D as 8.1% by difference to the 14.5% D&M figure in the Q4 deck
